subject.title: fix(cron): clean up recurring jobs converted to one-shot

question: Should recurring-to-`at` updates that omit `deleteAfterRun` deliberately adopt the existing create-time one-shot cleanup default, even when a stored recurring job has `deleteAfterRun: false`?
rationale: The patch changes the persisted lifecycle outcome of existing edited jobs; source establishes a strong create-time analogue, but acceptance of the upgrade behavior belongs to the code owner.

options.title: Accept target-schedule retention
options.body: Approve cleanup as the omitted default for recurring-to-one-shot conversions, matching new `at` job creation while preserving an explicit keep request.

options.title: Preserve stored retention
options.body: Keep legacy omitted-transition behavior and limit any new cleanup default to newly created one-shot jobs.

recommendation.title: Accept target-schedule retention
recommendation.body: Approve cleanup as the omitted default for recurring-to-one-shot conversions, matching new `at` job creation while preserving an explicit keep request.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the targeted lifecycle contract and transition coverage; a cron-area reviewer should confirm the upgrade choice.
